tasks.short: Arrange temporary staff through agencies, matching departmental needs, candidate suitability, availability and approved terms.

steps.what: Clarify temporary staffing needs with the hiring manager.
Check agency agreements, rates and purchasing requirements in the {PROCUREMENT}.
Send the staffing brief to selected agencies through the {EMAIL}.
Read agency replies and assemble candidate availability, experience and proposed rates.

loop.input: Agency replies and candidate CVs against staffing-brief fields.
loop.output: Source-linked availability, stated experience, rates and missing information; no ranking.
loop.check: Validate dates and rates deterministically; reviewer checks material facts against source passages.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per reply; unreadable or conflicting fields enter the exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Agency replies and CVs use inconsistent prose and layouts; structured portal fields should bypass extraction.

steps.what: Discuss candidates and choose a suitable temporary worker.
Negotiate availability, assignment conditions and rates with the agency.
Approve assignment cost and terms in the {PROCUREMENT}.
Confirm the approved assignment with the agency through the {EMAIL}.
Record the assignment and start date in the {HCM}.

tasks.design: A structured request in the {WORKFLOW} checks agency agreements in the {PROCUREMENT} and sends templated enquiries through the {EMAIL}. A bounded extraction loop prepares source-linked candidate facts for human selection and negotiation. Approval in the {PROCUREMENT} releases the exact agreed confirmation and creates the temporary worker record in the {HCM}; changed terms return for approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency replies vary, approval details sit in mailboxes, and purchasing and worker records use different identifiers. Native templates and approvals may already cover part of the work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing workflow configuration handles requests, approvals and messages. AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of building mappings and validation; bounded extraction handles varied replies.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent shortages, agency bargaining and candidate suitability need people. GDPR applies to candidate data; assess EU AI Act obligations if the intended use supports candidate evaluation, and consultation duties under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the department's real constraints, judge suitability and negotiate honestly when availability or terms change.

ambition.what: Temporary-cover planning for small departments without dedicated HR support.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time chasing replies and copying assignment details, and more time planning cover across departments. Hiring and spending authority stays with the existing approvers.

reach.task: Prepare temporary-worker onboarding from an approved assignment.
reach.learn: Required worker fields, start-date dependencies and duplicate-record checks.

reach.task: Review agency capacity and recurring temporary-staff demand.
reach.learn: Agency service measures, demand patterns and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Structured requests, templates, approval routing and record integration can automate coordination paperwork; this is a proposed design.
Textkernel parses CVs and matches candidates; this supports extraction feasibility, not the complete agency workflow.
AI used for recruitment or selection falls within the listed high-risk employment uses, subject to applicable classification rules.
GDPR Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.

assumptions: Agencies have existing agreements and identifiable contacts.
The workflow sends enquiries without committing expenditure.
Candidate comparison extracts facts without scoring or automatic exclusion.
Build ranges cover one initial business unit and existing systems; consultation may add elapsed time.
unknowns: Which agencies accept structured requests or provide portal access?
Which interfaces and configuration rights are available in the {PROCUREMENT} and {HCM}?
Who may approve assignments, and what constitutes a binding commitment?
Which national consultation requirements and candidate-data retention rules apply?
research_questions: Can native configuration cover enquiries, approvals and confirmations before custom code is needed?
How accurately can extraction preserve rates, availability and qualifications across representative replies?
Does the proposed extraction use trigger additional EU AI Act obligations in its actual deployment?
new_work: Review extracted candidate facts and resolve conflicting agency replies.
Maintain agency contacts, rate rules, templates and approval limits.
Handle failed confirmations, changed terms and duplicate worker records.
Review access, retention and integration logs.

tasks.short: Evaluate selection methods using hiring outcomes, research and manager feedback, then recommend changes.

steps.what: Agree which selection technique, population and outcomes to evaluate.
Export selection stages, decisions and hiring dates from the {ATS}.
Export scores and test versions from the testing platform {OTHER}.
Export agreed retention and probation outcomes from the {HCM}.
Join exports and resolve missing identifiers in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Read research and technical manuals relevant to the selection technique.

loop.input: A fixed set of accessible research papers and test manuals selected for the evaluation.
loop.output: Evidence table with population, method, findings, limitations and source passages.
loop.check: Verify every material claim against its cited passage; reviewer assesses relevance and research quality.
loop.stop: One pass and one repair per document; missing evidence stays marked unknown for human review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Research methods and limitations are expressed in varied prose; keyword matching cannot reliably extract their meaning.

steps.what: Discuss practical usefulness, candidate experience and observed problems.
Calculate outcome patterns and assess uncertainty in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Write a recommendation with supporting evidence, limitations and proposed changes.

loop.input: Reviewed findings, research evidence table and manager feedback.
loop.output: Recommendation draft separating measured findings, reported experience and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Match numbers to computed findings and claims to approved sources; HR reviews reasoning and limitations.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims are removed and unresolved recommendations return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template handles structure, but linking quantitative findings, research and conflicting feedback needs bounded prose synthesis.

steps.what: Decide whether to retain, investigate, change or withdraw the selection technique.

tasks.design: Scheduled exports from the {ATS}, testing platform {OTHER} and {HCM} create a restricted evaluation dataset in the {DATA_PLATFORM}, with deterministic joins and versioned calculations feeding the {BI}. Bounded loops prepare source-linked research tables and recommendation drafts in the {DOCS}. People interpret uncertainty, discuss practical effects and approve any change to selection methods.
tasks.previous_blocker: Candidate and employee records are hard to link, test versions are poorly tracked, and studies require careful reading. Repeatable analysis has often needed scarce analytical support.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building reusable joins, checks and statistical reports. Bounded reading and drafting loops can shorten evidence preparation without replacing methodological judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Small samples, selection bias and inconsistent probation ratings can make conclusions unreliable. GDPR purpose limitation, lawful access and national consultation rules constrain data use; assess EU AI Act duties if outputs influence selection or worker evaluation.
tasks.human_edge: Judge job relevance, distinguish correlation from useful validation, challenge weak evidence and weigh candidate experience alongside operational needs.

ambition.what: Selection-method evidence clinics for hiring managers.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more time investigating weak methods and advising managers, with repeatable evidence available between larger studies. They gain a stronger basis to recommend pilots or withdrawal; policy approval remains with the HR manager.

reach.role: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialist
reach.task: Connect selection criteria to documented job requirements.
reach.learn: Job analysis, criterion relevance and defensible competency definitions.

reach.task: Review whether a selection technique creates unjustified barriers.
reach.learn: Lawful equality analysis, accommodation needs and limits of small-group comparisons.

reach.task: Investigate whether onboarding differences explain early performance outcomes.
reach.learn: Learning exposure, outcome measurement and confounding factors.

evidence.claim: Versioned joins, fixed statistical calculations and dashboards can make recurring evaluation preparation repeatable; this is a proposed design.
Hiring-outcome correlations alone do not establish a selection technique's validity or causal effect.
Recruitment and worker-evaluation AI are listed high-risk employment uses; the deployment's intended purpose matters.
GDPR Article 22 applies to qualifying solely automated decisions; evaluation reports should not become automatic candidate decisions.
A documented report failure involving nonexistent sources supports checking generated research claims against original sources.

assumptions: This task evaluates selection methods rather than making individual hiring decisions.
The initial scope covers one technique and a defined hiring population.
Calculations follow an agreed analysis plan; qualified methodological support is available when needed.
Build ranges include access and consultation work but exclude waiting for future hiring outcomes.
unknowns: Are candidate-to-employee identifiers reliable and lawfully reusable for this purpose?
Are test versions, accommodations and outcome definitions recorded consistently?
Are samples large enough for the proposed analyses?
Which equality data can lawfully be used, and under which safeguards?
Who provides methodological review and approves selection-policy changes?
Which national consultation duties apply to the proposed data use?
research_questions: Which outcome measures provide credible evidence of job-relevant performance?
How should analysis account for rejected applicants having no observed employee outcomes?
Which calculations are justified at the available sample sizes?
Can existing reporting configuration supply the required extracts and audit trail?
What validation and documentation would the intended deployment require under the EU AI Act?
new_work: Resolve unmatched records and investigate changing data definitions.
Maintain test-version mappings, analysis specifications and access controls.
Verify research passages and review generated recommendations.
Monitor sample adequacy, uncertainty and inappropriate reuse of reports.
Track approved pilots and check whether their outcomes support the original recommendation.

role.altitude: HR specialists move from coordination paperwork and one-off evidence gathering toward staffing advice and selection-method evaluation. Hiring, spending and policy decisions retain explicit human owners.
reach: Support HR assistants with reliable assignment-to-onboarding handoffs.
Work with job analysis specialists on defensible selection criteria.
Work with equal opportunity representatives on barriers and lawful evaluation.
Help HR managers compare agency capacity and selection-method evidence.
skills_to_grow: Structured staffing briefs and agency negotiation
Workflow configuration, data mapping and exception handling
Statistical uncertainty, selection bias and research appraisal
GDPR purpose limitation and applicable employment AI obligations
role.ambitious_version: Provide a shared staffing advisory service that helps smaller departments plan temporary cover and helps hiring managers choose defensible selection methods.
